NASA recently highlighted a rare astronomical event happening this December: a Christmas Eve Supermoon.

On December 24th, 2026, the full Moon will coincide with the Moon’s closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit, creating what’s known as a supermoon. A supermoon occurs when a full Moon aligns closely with perigee the point in the Moon’s orbit where it is closest to Earth.

What makes this event especially notable is that it falls on Christmas Eve. The last full Moon to occur on December 24th was in 1996.
